# Bestiary

*Pages PDF 140-157*

## **Bestiary**
# **Sea Monsters Great and Small and Several Grand Captains**
The seas of the world are populated by many fell beasts, from the dreaded Black Leviathan to the legendary Kraken. These great beasts sometimes rise to the surface from the blackest depths of the ocean, attracted by the churning waters of a sea battle. Often as large as the biggest ships, these towering monstrosities come to join the carnage in an orgy of mindless destruction. Their razor-sharp fangs slash and bite, and their great jaws cut through flesh, wood, and steel with ease. Those sailors unlucky enough to fall overboard are doomed, consumed in an instant by these ravening monsters from the deeps. 

## Creature Trait: Grim (Rating)
If, at the beginning of its turn, this creature does not have at least its Grim Rating in Advantage points, its Advantage pool immediately increases to its Grim Rating. If the creature currently has a _Entangled_ , _Surprised_ , or _Unconscious_ Condition, it does not gain this Advantage. 

If using the Group Advantage rules from **Up in Arms,** the creature generates its Grim Rating in Advantage for the Adversary Advantage Pool. 

## Creature Trait: Marine Creature
The creature is at home in the ocean and unsuited to life on land. The profiles of such creatures assume that they are in an aquatic environment and they move their full M in water. If they are removed from the water, their M drops to 1 and all Tests they make suffer from –2 SL. 

Creatures with the _Marine Creature_ Trait need to be moist to breathe properly. If they are removed from the water, they must be regularly doused with water or they will begin to suffocate as described in **WFRP** , page 181. 

## **Lurkerfish**
These hideous fish are not marine creatures, but sailors on the Sea of Claws know to be wary of them lurking in the fjords of Norsca and the waters of rivers such as the Salz, Lynsk, and Sannez. The Lurkerfish hides in the mud and weeds close to riverbanks, with its stocky body just under the water. 

They use their peculiar glowing head fin to attract riverside animals. The slowly waving appendage has a hypnotic quality; even intelligent creatures can be beguiled by the luminous lure. With their powerful tail fins, they launch themselves at their prey, aiming to grab on, ripping flesh and gulping blood. They can survive out of water for a while, dropping off a fleeing animal and flopping their way back to the riverbank. If a person dares eat a Lurkerfish, they taste delicious. 

**Lure of the Lurkerfish:** The gently oscillating bluegreen lights seen by the riverbank at dusk and dawn are sometimes mistaken for fireflies. Any Character passing a **Hard (–20) Lore (Riverways)** Test will know that these are likely to be the lures of Lurkerfish. Those who fail the Lore Test must make an **Easy (+40) Cool** Test or become beguiled by the sight and unable to perform any action except moving towards the light — effectively acquiring the _Unconscious_ Condition.

## **Gymmcrab**
An adult Gymmcrab grows big as a dog, with a carapace bearing a skull-like marking, and large, scarlet, polypous eyes. Native to Norsca, younger and smaller Gymmcrabs form hazardous swarms, able to climb ropes trailing from ships or clamber atop one another, building living stairs to surmount obstacles. Their lifecycle can prove hazardous to shipping, as their young form barnacle-like clusters that can foul the hull of a ship, while the adult crabs haunt the beaches, scavenging flesh. Experienced in fighting one another, they often attempt to disarm or grapple opponents. They make excellent eating.

## **Latch-Eel**
Latch-eels are sinuous creatures growing up to four feet in length. They are deep aquamarine in colour, with powerful grasping jaws. They feed by latching onto their victims, tying themselves into a knot, finding purchase against their own bodies, and creating enough leverage to rip chunks from their victim. Adult Latch-eels are known to be strong enough to tear away armour. They can also exude slime, making them impossible to grapple. A sticky slime cloud may clog a victim’s nose (or gills) causing suffocation. Mothers are often accompanied by a swarm of foot-long young.

If it succeeds, it produces a clump of slime, benefiting from +4 SL to subsequent Tests to break free. The opponent must make a **Challenging (+0) Athletics** Test. Failure means that slime has covered their face, and the opponent must either release the Latch-eel or start to suffer suffocation ( **WFRP** , page 181). 

## **Daggerfish**
Daggerfish are a species of flying fish. Adults are about twelve inches in length, with a wing-fin-span of about eighteen. The fish is named for the razor-edged spines projecting from the edges of its fin tips. Their ability to leap from the water up to a height of four feet, often in large shoals, makes them physically dangerous, as their spines are sharp enough to slice through cloth and flesh. Although this usually only poses a problem for rafts, rowboats, and other vessels that lie low in the water, there is evidence of unusually large Daggerfish leaping high enough to land on large ships. 

Although Daggerfish prefer warmer waters, they do appear in the Sea of Claws during the summer. They are edible and tasty, and can be caught in nets as they leap from the water. They are attracted to bright lights, so they are usually fished on nights without moonlight by fishermen in shallow boats bearing lanterns. Those unfamiliar with the risk of the Daggerfish’s attraction to light can place themselves in danger, as a large shoal will repeatedly leap from the water.

## **Sea Elemental**
According to scholars of magic, the Jade Wind of _Ghyran_ bears a certain equivalence to water. Those with the Sight can see it fall to the earth like rain, flow along with brooks and rivers, and collect in pools. It is no great surprise then that the oceans of the world contain within them great quantities of _Ghyran_ . 

_Ghyran_ does not diffuse throughout the waters of the seas. The Wind may move like water, but within the great oceans it becomes locally concentrated, drifting together _Ghyran_ can lead to a in clumps. These intensities of flourishing of life, dense mats of seaweed or swarms of undulating jellyfish. 

Where _Ghyran_ becomes most concentrated, the waters that bear it can become animated, forming the rough outline of a gigantic humanoid form. Stories of such Sea Elementals excite much debate among the magisters of the Jade College. Some theorise that they have some kinship with the Naiads, being a spirit of nature manifested as living water. Others speculate that they are Incarnate Elementals of _Ghyran_ . As of yet, no rite has been developed enabling a wizard to summon a Sea Elemental, though some wizards claim to have bent them to their will for a short period of time. 

**Immersion:** The Sea Elemental may attempt to immerse its opponents by making a Grapple. If the Sea Elemental _Entangled_ Condition on its opponent, it draws inflicts an them into its own body. 

The immersed character suffers from Suffocation as detailed on **WFRP** , page 181. They may attempt to escape by freeing themselves from the _Entangled_ Condition as if they were Grappled by the Sea Elemental, making Opposed Strength Tests against its Strength of 59 to break free. However, the Sea Elemental does not need to actively maintain the Grapple — it may act as if the immersed character were not there and does not count as being Engaged. 

**Fire Resistant:** _Ablaze_ Sea Elementals never suffer from Conditions. 

**Mindless Spellcaster:** Sea Elementals may use their Strength Characteristic for the purpose of casting spells and channelling. 

A wild Sea Elemental is a frightening prospect. Infused with the Wind of Life they may be, but they are not nurturing or gentle in their temperaments. They are boisterous and violent, exuberant in their own strength and vitality to the detriment of those in their way. They seem to delight in acts of destruction, smashing ships and summoning whirlpools. They fall upon sailors with a rapacious frenzy, catching them up in the churning waters of their own bodies and drowning them therein.

## **Gargantuan**
The Gargantuan is a sinuous beast many hundreds of feet in length. Its body is immensely powerful and muscular, reaching a diameter of up to ten yards. According to the Elves of Ulthuan there is only one Gargantuan, which has dwelled in the depths since the dawn of the world. 

On occasion, voyagers have sworn that they have seen the enormous serpent swimming after shoals of fish, swinging its maw side to side as it seeks to satisfy its appetite. 

Such reports are rare. Perhaps this is because, as the Elves suggest, the Gargantuan really is the sole survivor of a species that once thrived before the coming of Chaos — but a grimmer truth is that the Gargantuan is a belligerent and cruel creature that is just as pleased to shatter a ship and devour its crew as to swallow a swarm of krill. The Gargantuan’s preferred method of attack is to approach its prey from below, wrap its sinuous coils around the victim, and crush the life from it. Should the prey prove too obstreperous, the Gargantuan resorts to another form of attack: its vast muscular body can deliver a powerful jolt of electricity to anything caught within its coils. 

**Electrical Discharge:** If the creature successfully Grapples an opponent, then at the start of its subsequent turns, the creature can spend 1 Advantage to deliver an electric shock to the Grappled character. The electrical discharge inflicts a hit of 10 Damage which ignores nonmagical metal armour. Any Character taking Wounds from the electrical attack must also pass a **Difficult (–10) Endurance** Test or suffer a _Stunned_ Condition. 

The Gargantuan cannot make electrical attacks with impunity. Each time it uses the attack, it must make an **Average (+20) Endurance** Test. Failure indicates that it _Fatigued_ Condition. suffers a 

_Fatigued_ Whilst the Gargantuan is under the effects of a Condition, electrical discharge attacks only inflict Damage 6 hits which ignore non-magical metal armour. 

The Gargantuan may also discharge electricity when it has _Grappled_ a boat. This does no damage against the boat, but the crew all receive a jolt, suffering a Damage 6 hit (reduced to a Damage 3 hit if the Gargantuan has a _Fatigued_ Condition).

To constrict a vessel, it must spend one turn wrapping itself about the vessel for every 10 points of Size the vessel possesses. Once the vessel is wrapped up, the Gargantuan starts to squeeze — making an Extended Opposed Strength Test against the boat’s Toughness. Once the SL reaches the boat’s Wounds, the boat shatters, reduced to a mass of flotsam. 

During this time, the boat’s crew may attack the Gargantuan or attempt to lever it from the boat. Attacks that inflict more than 7 Wounds may cause the Gargantuan to let go if it fails a subsequent **Average (+20) Cool** Test. Levering the Gargantuan requires making an Opposed Strength Test against the creature. A result of 0 to 4 SL prevents it from squeezing the boat that turn, and a result of 5 SL or more forces it to release the boat. 

## **Kharibdyss**
The Kharibdyss is not native to the Sea of Claws. These beasts haunt the cold and murky deeps around the shores of Naggaroth, far to the west. They are horrific creatures, slow-witted but powerful. Their stocky, hulking bodies sprout a crown of five flailing tentacles, four of which terminate in rudimentary heads, atavistic to the point of being almost vestigial, little more than mouths with basic senses of taste and smell, specialised in seeking out and consuming prey. The fifth, central head is larger and more complex, housing the creature’s minute brain. It is equipped with a long and winding lower jaw lined with hundreds of sharp fangs. The Kharibdyss uses this coiling jaw to rasp apart larger prey creatures, spraying about chunks of gore and flesh to be gobbled up by the smaller heads. The creature has a voracious appetite, and ferociously efficient digestive enzymes that can dissolve flesh, metal, and bone in a matter of minutes. 

The Dark Elves of Naggaroth have learned various techniques to direct the Kharibdyss, and are known to goad it into battle as a beast of war. Since the destruction of the Black Ark _Cleaver of Souls,_ there have been numerous reports of attacks by slimy multi-headed sea monsters preying on the island communities of Odner and Lugern. Master Stefan Ellendan, Professor of Sciences at the University of Salzenmund, has conjectured that several of the beasts were dismembered during the destruction of the Dark Elf vessel, and that each piece has grown into a separate adult. This has led to a false belief amongst the scholars of Nordland that the creature has powerful regenerative qualities, and the more prosaic truth of the matter — that a breeding pair escaped to spawn — has been overlooked. 

Those who live by the sea are sadly unaware that dry land offers no sanctuary from the Kharibdyss, for whilst the creature is at home in the ocean, it rampages wherever hunger leads it. Its slimy body, adapted to resist the fantastic pressures of the ocean, possesses incredible strength and fortitude. Whilst it is by no means agile out of the water, its webbed feet can nevertheless propel the Kharibdyss forward at a surprising turn of speed. The creature is also noted for the howling it makes when excited. Survivors of its attacks often mention that the most disturbing thing about the Kharibdyss is that its calls possess a strange plangency, like those of a human in the throes of anguish.

## **Merwyrm**
The Sea of Claws is a notorious haunt of Merwyrms. They are large creatures, rivalling the great baleen whales for length. They possess long serpentine bodies, covered in a layer of thick scales and corded with taut sinew and tough bunched muscles. However, they are not true Sea Serpents, for if the need calls for it, they can waddle forth from the water on four stubby limbs, each tipped with razor-sharp claws. 

Scholars suggest that the Merwyrms represent a lineage possessing the characteristics of both Sea Serpents and Dragons, and which is ancestral to both. They speculate that the scaled forms of Merwyrms swarmed in the primordial oceans of the world and reached proportions that rival the vast Leviathans. There may be truth to these accounts, but if so, the Merwyrms are much diminished in size and population. 

The Asur of Cothique and Lothern claim to practice a form of Sea Magic far more powerful than that taught in Marienburg. Their mages, known as Storm Weavers, are said to have formed pacts with Merwyrms, and the beasts are reported to accompany fleets of High Elven warships. 

To those who make their living by the Sea of Claws, the creatures are a source of terror. When food is scarce, they have been known to assault coastal communities, devouring the inhabitants. Whilst they prefer to remain in the ocean, they are fully capable of venturing forth on the land. They are fierce fighters and their powerful regenerative qualities mean that a single monster is more than capable of wiping out whatever ragtag defenders might stand between it and a Nordland fishing village. 

## **Syreen**
Tales tell of the Syreens, whose call lures sailors to their deaths on the rocks. They are said to be a form of Banshee that haunts the seas. When a witch is drowned it is said that her soul persists as an anguished shade. The souls of witches reliably take on such ghostly shapes because they fear punishments that await them in the Realm of Morr, or it may be that they are so infused with _Dhar_ that they return as spectres. 

The Sarl Norse are suspected of throwing petty magic users into the waves to create stretches of coastline haunted by Syreens. On the other side of the Great Ocean, the Vampire Arch Grand Commodore Luthor Harken is also aware of the rites needed to create a Syreen, and seeks witches to drown and bind them to his navy of the dead.

## **Bone Hydra**
On rare occasions, the corpses of sea creatures drift into such areas where the malign magic of sunken warpstone can corrupt and reanimate them. 

The Bone Hydra is such a beast. It is not the skeleton of a true Hydra (insomuch as such creatures of Chaos can be considered in any way ‘true’ in the first place) for it only possesses three heads. Each of these heads is vast. Some scholars suggest that the Bone Hydra was once a multi-headed Sea Dragon. Master Stefan Ellendan of the University of Salzenmund suggests that it is a form of Lustrian giant crocodile, and that it came to be mutated only post-mortem. 

The Bone Hydra is not native to the Sea of Claws, instead haunting the area known as the Galleon’s Graveyard far out to sea. But with the Chaos Wastes and forlorn land of Norsca so close, beasts of equivalent strangeness lurk under the waves.

## **Leech Wyrm**
Another inhabitant of those areas of the sea floor corrupted by concentrations of _Dhar_ is the Chasm Leech. These huge worms are not, in and of themselves, fierce animals. Their mouthparts are lined with rasping teeth, but the leeches are sluggish and soft-bodied, and in order for them to ingest the flesh that makes up their diet, that meat must already be well on the way to putrefaction. 

However, when Chasm Leeches locate a corpse, they worm their way inside the body and multiply. A corpse infested with Chasm Leeches may start to move once again, the Leeches replacing the sinew and muscle of the decayed creature with their own bodies. Now that they have a host, the Leeches are dangerous — to sustain their lifecycle, they must send more corpses to the depths. 

Leech Wyrms are the animated corpses of Sea Dragons that have been swept into the depths and infested with Chasm Leeches. The Sea Dragon is the preferred host of the Leeches, for it possesses enough flesh to keep them fed for many years, whilst providing them with a powerful and massive body capable of slaying other creatures for the next generation of Leeches to inhabit.

## **Orb Leviathan and Black Leviathan**
There are several species of Leviathan in the oceans of the world. They have in common the fact that they are bony fish whose heads and loins are protected by heavy scales. They are all voracious predators. 

The Orb Leviathan is pale in colour and swathed in a fatty layer like the blubber of a seal. It is a small species, with full-grown adults reaching a mere 45 yards in length. The creature is ungainly, with a slow metabolism, suited for life in the depths of the coldest oceans. During chilly winters, they are sometimes sighted in the Sea of Claws. Unsuited for active hunting, the beast bears a luminous lure that waves back and forth upon a tendril in front of its gaping upturned mouth. Master Stefan Ellendan, Professor of Sciences at the University of Salzenmund, has speculated that the Orb Leviathan is the true adult form of the Lurkerfish, but whilst their lures do work in similar ways, the beasts are entirely separate species. 

The greatest of these fish is the Black Leviathan, a huge, carnivorous deep-sea fish, with a cavernous mouth full of barbed fangs, and scales thicker than the hull of a Greatship. Whilst the Black Leviathan makes its lair in the depths of the sea, it hunts on the surface. Its habit is to approach suitable prey by swimming low in the water. As it closes, it rises from the waves, vast maw agape, and gulps its victim down whole. The measurements of the Black Leviathan are a popular subject of debate amongst scholars. Master Ellendan claims to have conducted a meta-analysis of reports of Black Leviathan sightings and supposes the average specimen to be _‘four furlongs and two chains from foretusk to tail tip’_ .

## **Triton**
No creature in the world excites quite as much legend and speculation as Triton. Despite the fascination he excites in mariners, scholars, wizards, and priests alike, there is little that can be said about his nature that does not elicit fiery controversy. 

He is rarely seen, but is reported to range throughout the seas of the world. He bears a resemblance to the winsome Sirens that are occasionally glimpsed darting about the islands of the Tilean Sea. Above the waist, he is shaped much like a man, with a powerful frame and handsome, if savage, visage. He has a thick mane of hair, and a heavy, shaggy beard. Below his navel he has the loins and tail of a fish. He is also truly titanic; even the vast Bonecrusher Giants are dwarfed by mighty Triton. 

Whilst he is undoubtedly monstrous, there are signs that Triton is more than a mere beast. He bears accoutrements in the form of a spiked crown, and a vast trident capable of impaling the hull of the largest ships. Both items are made from a strange metal that is hard as iron, and incorruptible as gold. Where these artefacts can have come from is a mystery — no worldly forge is large enough to have produced them. 

Triton is master of several mysterious powers, able to control the elements and tame the monsters of the deep. His abilities share common ground with the practice of Sea Magic and the Miracles performed by priests of Manann. Yet despite such evidence of intelligence and sophistication, he has never been known to communicate with mariners. Whilst he does make arcane utterances when conjuring his spells, if he speaks a language, it is not one recognised by Elves or wizards. 

A faction amongst the Loremasters of Saphery claim that Triton dwelled within the ocean before the coming of Chaos, and that he taught their own forebears the skills of sailing and navigation. They say he was once smaller, but communicative and cooperative. When Chaos entered the world it altered Triton, causing him to grow greatly in size and strength, but robbing him of either the ability, or the inclination, to speak. 

Another theory has it that Triton was unaffected by Chaos, and that his reticence is due to the great offence he takes at the temerity of sailors who plunder the seas for food and whale oil. Triton does seem to bear some affection for the creatures of the ocean, as evidenced by the history of hostility he has shown towards Dark Elves, whose subjugation of Kharibdyss and Sea Dragons seems to rouse his ire. 

To the Humans of the Old World, Triton is believed to share some relationship to Manann, though folktales and apocryphal testaments have it that he is variously the sea god’s son, brother, avatar, first follower, or divine servant. The Elves suppose the matter is not so simple, for the Druchii honour Mathlann (the Elven deity whose domain and nature share a great deal with those of Manann) as earnestly as do the seafarers of Cothique, and still Triton bears them murderous resentment.

**Triton’s Sea Magic:** Triton is a potent spellcaster, but he does not cast magic like any other being in the world. His spellcraft blurs the lines between miracles of the gods and mastery of the Aethyr. Triton knows the following Sea Magics (see page 15): _Living Mire, Whirlpool, Sea of Glass._ 

He may cast the following Miracles of Manann as if they were spells with a CN of 1: _Becalm, Fair Winds, Sea Curse, Rip Tides_ . He may also cast the following Miracle of Stromfels as if it were a spell with a CN of 1: _Raging Seas_ . If Triton generates additional SL when casting these Miracles as spells, he may use the overcasting rules to adjust them as if they were spells. 

**Favoured of Manann:** Triton’s exact relationship with Manann is mysterious but undeniable. How this manifests is left up to the GM, but Triton will not likely respond positively to a vessel that has a negative Manann’s Mood, and may treat a ship with a Manann’s Mood of 50 or more with respect. Conversely, if Triton is disrespected, Manann’s Mood may decrease, and if he is pleased, Manann’s Mood may improve. 

**Lord of the Deeps:** Triton’s Charm Animal Skill and _Animal Affinity_ Talent may only be employed in relation to marine creatures. However, criteria that might normally prevent a Character utilising the Charm Animal Skill do not apply to Triton — belligerent, territorial, trained, or wounded sea creatures still afford him respect. Only marine creatures that have been magically dominated fail to respect the dominance of Triton. 

Creatures with the _Amphibious_ or _Aquatic_ Traits are subject to this rule when they are in the water but may ignore it on land.

## **Captain Jaego Roth[–] Sartosan Privateer**
Captain Jaego Roth is considered the greatest privateer of the age. The son of famed Sartosan cartographer and explorer Indigio Roth, the young Jaego spent his life aboard ship, journeying with his father to places uncharted by any of Sartosa’s other far-ranging freebooters. When the elder Roth was at last forced to retire after losing both legs to a Sea Giant, Jaego set out to forge his own legacy. 

Aboard his ship _The Nightwatch_ , Jaego Roth has sailed from the ice-clogged northern seas all the way to Lustria’s fog-shrouded shores. Following his father’s maps, Jaego brought back treasures the likes of which few others had seen, adding them to plunder taken preying upon other vessels. His fame grew so great that soon there was no shortage of people looking to hire his services as a naval commander, and he has sailed in the fleets of Tilea, Bretonnia, and the Empire. After each victory, Jaego returned to his family with his holds laden with riches. 

Then, in a single night, he lost everything. Jaego returned to Sartosa to find the Rusting Harbour ablaze. Those who tell the tale say this was the first, and only, time the great privateer knew fear. Jaego battled his way through the flames, desperate to reach his father’s ship, _The Enlightenment_ , where his family lived. By the time he forced his way aboard, he was too late. In his son’s room, he found only two charred corpses. 

As he stumbled away, barely noticing the smoke catching in his lungs, one final horror greeted him. His father’s body lay on the deck. The old sailor had dragged himself out into the night air before the heat and smoke finally claimed him. From all the countless treasures of his adventures, the mapmaker had chosen only three things to save: a moondial; a telescope; and a map, pinned to the inside of a turtle’s shell. 

Ever since that night, Jaego has been a changed man. Those who knew him before say it is as though a light died in his eyes, replaced with something cold and determined. The survivors his crew found babbled strange stories of the attack — a ghost ship crewed by spectres; a great kraken that screamed with a sound like tortured metal; a floating hulk, made up of countless wrecked ships. One name emerged from the confused accounts, however: Noctilus, the vampire lord of the mythical Galleon’s Graveyard. Most dismissed these tales out of hand. Jaego, however, latched onto them like a drowning man to a piece of driftwood. 

Captain Roth spent little time recuperating before he ordered _The Nightwatch_ make sail. He would find the vampire. He would find wherever it called home. And he would put it to the torch. He now searches for any information on the creature, hoarding scraps of stories like a miser with their gold. The three relics his father died protecting sit constantly upon his desk, and Jaego has lost countless hours puzzling over their meaning. The Galleon’s Graveyard had become an obsession of his father’s, a story told repeatedly by a man losing his wits to age. Or so Jaego had thought. But if these artefacts hold the means to finding it, the solution to their riddle has so far eluded his efforts. 

His quest has recently taken him to the Sea of Claws and the Empire’s coast. While he is no closer to finding the Graveyard itself, Captain Roth is no fool. To kill a vampire, especially one as powerful as Noctilus, will take far more than he and his crew can bring to bear. Roth is calling in every favour he has ever earned, seeking audiences with barons, wizards, and even Elector Counts. He has heard the Temple of Sigmar might hold the means to his revenge, and he has plans to bring his plight to the Grand Theogonist in Altdorf. This will be no easy feat, however. Altdorf lies at the heart of the Empire, and to travel down the Reik will mean passing through Marienburg, where traders have reason to hate the name Roth.

## **Long Drong Slayer[–] Captain of the Slayer Pirates**
_‘From Grimnir’s Halls I’ll shoot at ye, ye bastard!’_ 

— Long Drong Slayer 

Long Drong Slayer, leader of the Slayer Pirates, is one of Sartosa’s most well-respected captains, though this may be akin to the respect one gives a barrel of blackpowder. No other sailor would willingly go where Long Drong ventures, chasing down the ocean’s most terrifying monsters in his voyage to a worthy death. 

Long Drong (so called for his great height among Dwarfs) was once a seafarer from Barak Varr. He never sought the adventuring life. Serving as captain of _The Barrel of Ale_ , he transported the best brews to thirsty Dwarfs wherever he made port. ‘Slow and steady’ was Long Drong’s maxim, and he gained a reputation as a safe pair of hands. That was until a storm drove _The Barrel_ onto Sartosa’s cliffs. Only by Long Drong’s quick thinking did the crew escape. However, they were forced to leave their beloved ship impaled upon the rocks, its precious cargo bleeding into the waves. For Long Drong, this was a shame beyond bearing. He and his fellows took the Slayer’s Oath and set out to find what doom Sartosa held. 

His first action was to storm the stronghold of the pirate lord Capitano Sissico. Hearing stories of the vicious tyrant, Drong thought here would be his chance to claim a worthy death. Unfortunately, it was not to be. What he did get was a fortress to call home, Sissico’s parrot (which he named Bitsy due to its habit of saying ‘bits o’ gold’), Sissico’s ship, and enough plundered booty to turn it into something a Dwarf could be proud to sail. _The Fair Fregar_ is now a testament to Dwarf engineering, instantly recognisable by its figurehead, forged in the semblance of a beautiful Dwarf maid. This also doubles as a battering ram. 

The Slayer Pirates have gained repute as skilled warriors, joining the ranks of mercenary companies from Tilea to the Empire. They are experts at capturing the pay chests used to pay rival mercenary armies, breaking the line of elite soldiers guarding them with a frenzied barrage of pistol shots and insults. For this they are well-compensated, Long Drong having lost none of his business savvy. In truth though, their mercenary work is just to keep them in rum and blackpowder. Their true focus, the thing which will send _The Fair Fregar_ charging off to all corners of the world, is fighting sea monsters. 

Long Drong has not yet met a monster he could not best. _The Fair Fregar’s_ flanks bear scoring from battles with a Leviathan, while scraps of scaled Merwyrm hide fly beneath his signature flagon and crossed pistols banner. Such victories are hard won. Drong lost a hand to a Lurkerfish, a leg to a Sea Drake, and an eye to a bet (long story). His doom has eluded him, though he takes satisfaction knowing many of his crew have regained honour in his service, their places taken by others seeking death on the sea. 

Those pirate captains of Sartosa who occasionally join Long Drong for drinks describe a darkness creeping over him. Drong still drinks and sings chanties, shouting out stories of his latest victories to roars of approval. But, as the night wears on, a melancholy mood settles upon him. He sits at his table, rubbing the curve of his hook and staring out to sea. Drong knows he cannot keep up this hunt forever. How much longer does he have before he is robbed of a worthy end?

## **Wulfrik[–] Champion of the Sarl**
All Norscan longships strike terror into those who live their lives along the coast. Yet there is one which even the bravest have learned to dread. Upon its sail it carries the ever-turning wheel of the Ruinous Powers, daubed in dried blood. Heads, each taken from a foe bested in single combat, line its prow. Its oars scull the waves in unison, pushing the ship on in time to the sound of the skaldchanters singing a single name: _Wulfrik_ . 

A giant of a man, Wulfrik is the most feared and celebrated champion of the Sarl. He sails the Sea of Claws and beyond, raiding and slaughtering to bring fresh glory to his name — and to the gods, of course. He carries their mark upon his flesh, an indicator to any who cross his path that here is someone worthy of the gods’ attention. And, as far as Wulfrik is concerned, they are right. 

Though still a young man, Wulfrik has led his raiders to countless victories along the southern coasts, bringing back loot to swell the Sarl king’s coffers and leaving only hollow-eyed survivors and burned ruins in his wake. From Bretonnia to Kislev, peasants and warriors alike have wound up decorating his ship. With each new success, a fresh verse is added to his saga. The tales of his exploits have now made their way throughout all of Norsca, though no one recounts them with more enthusiasm than Wulfrik himself. 

Instead, he lashed him to the prow of his longship to serve as a grim figurehead. The man screamed for three days before finally dying. 

Nothing brings Wulfrik more joy than besting other champions in single combat. There is something wonderful, he says as the mead flows each night, about driving your enemy’s greatest and bravest into the dirt and seeing their companions falter as they realise, truly realise, there is nothing they can do to stave off death. His boasting and rapid rise have allowed him endless chances to indulge in this recreation. Whenever he anchors in Kirkjugarður Langskipa, champions from all across the Norscan lands, and even some from more distant places, arrive to challenge the young upstart. Those who offer Wulfrik a decent fight are sometimes offered the chance to join his crew. Those who don’t will serve aboard Kotfotr in a different, decorative capacity. 

However, even as Wulfrik’s reputation grows, so does his arrogance. There is little to challenge him now, he says. So many of the gods’ greatest champions have already fallen to his blades that he is forced to search further afield. He hunts down rumours of great warriors almost as eagerly as he does plunder, knowing the more his reputation grows, the greater his power will one day be. Wulfrik has ambitions. He does not intend to spend his days in fruitless pursuit of some frivolous god’s favour. They know they have chosen well in him, and he will bring them greater glory still if they let him achieve what he wants. 

One story tells how he and his fellows came upon a Bretonnian galleon as it lay becalmed in the empty sea. The gods watched over their champion as Wulfrik drove his ship Kotfotr — _The Hunter’s Claw_ — through the hail of cannon fire, hollering his challenge to the noble who commanded the great vessel. The noble, however, refused, hiding in the bowels of the galleon and leaving his own crew to die. Wulfrik hunted him through those dark spaces for close to an hour, and when he finally dragged the coward to light, he refused to grant him an honourable death. 

The chiefs and kings of the Norscan people are growing weak, too focused on scrabbling for power among themselves. The time has come for a new leader. One who all men will look to and know as a worthy champion. For Wulfrik, the greatest treasure is his saga. The more his legend grows, the more warriors flock to his banner, the more the chiefs learn to fear his name. One day, Wulfrik will prove himself greater than all of them. This is the destiny the gods have set before him. What else could they have in mind for someone as mighty as Wulfrik?

## **Arch-Sealord Vrisk Ironscratch**
Vrisk Ironscratch is Arch-Sealord of Clan Skurvy. He was present at the Great Summoning of 2302 IC, and boldly placed his paw upon the Black Pillar of Commandments and earned the right to sit on the Council of Thirteen. His ascension was a surprise to many, for Clan Skurvy were by no means a major power in Skavendom. 

The Great Summoning, and its aftermath, instilled in the Skaven a common purpose, and Vrisk was quick to think of a niche to occupy. He proposed, given that most of his clan’s holdings comprised the warrens that riddled the cliffs beneath the city of Tobaro, that Clan Skurvy be granted a generous stipend in warptokens to design and construct an effective navy. 

After much bickering, the Council devoted a generous portion of resources to Vrisk. The humble station of Clan Skurvy probably contributed to his fortunes — by awarding him a fortune in warptokens, his fellow councillors denied each other a generous windfall that might upset the balance of power. Better a small clan receive assistance than a major clan come to dominate its rivals. In winning the stipend, Vrisk also had to make several promises to purchase weaponry and specialist soldiers from Clans Skryre, Moulder, Eshin, and Pestilens. It ought also to be noted that Seerlord Kritislik strongly objected to the construction of a navy, claiming it would be too overt and leave evidence to be found by the enemies of the Skaven, so the other councillors may have voted in its favour simply to annoy the Seerlord. 

Thanks to this (conditional) generosity on behalf of the Council, Clan Skurvy were granted the resources to gnaw out the Undercity lair of Spineport, hidden in caves carved from the Tobaran coast by storms. In 2321 IC, strange, ramshackle craft were spotted on the Tilean sea, and the Dwarfs of Barak Varr reported sinking several vessels manned by Skaven sailors. In less than two decades, Vrisk had done much to keep his promise to the Council. 

Clan Skurvy are now a serious maritime threat. The clan’s ramshackle fleet reaps a fortune from piracy, much of which is spent on press-ganging new captives to work the treadmills that power their ships. 

Their spoils are also supplemented by salvaging wrecks off the coast of the Isle of Sirens, bounty that is hauled back to Spineport. The Skaven tend not to attack vessels near the coast, for they are wary of proving Seerlord Kritislik right. For his part, Vrisk is an active participant in the operations of his clan. On board a clanship, every Skaven is a suspect of mutiny — which is just as well, as they are all planning to do it sooner or later. Vrisk’s clawcaptains struggle to maintain order, so the arch-sealord himself deems fit to keep a watch from the prow of Clan Skurvy’s flagship, _The Teeth of Spineport_ , a seething hulk bedecked in Warp Lightning Naval Cannons. 

Vrisk occupies the eighth seat on the Council of Thirteen. It is a humble position, and Vrisk rarely engages in the intrigue necessary to win greater power. He is said to disdain the rancorous competition of Skavenblight in favour of a life on the ocean wave. Also, if he did not devote his energies to leading his clan in person, half of them would mutiny by sundown.

|The Teeth of<br>Spineport|75|5 (25)|–|60|55|200|1000|–|

_The Teeth of Spineport_ mounts 10 Warp Lightning Naval Cannon on its deck, five facing port and five facing starboard. 

**Treadmill:** Boat Handling Tests are made using the Captain’s Intimidate Skill rather than Sail or Row. The Treadmill works in much the same way as Oars, but the Treadmill has the ability to move a ship in reverse as well as forward. Should the Captain of a ship with a Treadmill wish to reverse direction, they must make a **Challenging (+0) Leadership** Test or a **Challenging (+0) Intimidate** Test. If the Test is passed, from the following round onwards, the ship may move backwards.
